localised_description: Sinope, the jewel of the Black Sea coast, is held by the Greeks. Whoever holds it controls the trade between Anatolia and the northern lands. Sultan Kaykaus has resolved to take it, so that Seljuk caravans may reach the sea in the north as they already do at Attaleia in the south.

Kipchak raiders and Rus princes trouble the merchants of the Crimea, and Seljuk goods sold at Sinope must cross the sea to reach them. The Sultan orders an expedition across the Black Sea to seize the trading ports of the Crimea, as his armies did at Sudak.
